content.comment_body: Hello all, I'm setting up a small facility using 2x [product_name] (with [article_no]) and 2x [product_name] modules. I have three switches to control with LEDs to show when the lights are on. I'm using an output from [product_name] to drive an LED indicator (230V in the switch). The issue is there's a residual 1V on the output of [product_name]—is this normal? Also, I plan to connect four automatic switches (motion sensors) to [product_name]. Any advice for wiring or configuration? Thanks and sorry for any language mistakes.

Hi [user_name], If you're referring to '1V present on output when off,' this is typical, and if it's problematic for your setup, you can add a resistor to pull it down. For the motion sensors, could you clarify the wiring scheme? For instance, if it's a three-wire sensor (+24VDC, output, 0V), or you could share the motion sensor catalogue for precise advice.

Thank you for your reply. I'm surprised about the 1V on the relay output of the [product_name] ([article_no]), as that's not documented—but adding a resistor works for me. Regarding the motion detector, here's the details: [url]. It's a two-wire device without neutral, and requires a minimum load of 40W. I'll try adding a capacitor rated at 2.5kV 100nF and test it tomorrow. Best regards, [user_name]

Lack of clear documentation regarding electrical behavior and wiring options caused confusion.
